claim.claim-text: a host interface (304); and a network interface (310), wherein the network interface (310) includes a transmit portion (312) and a receive portion (316), wherein the transmit portion (312) comprises a first set of data paths and wherein the receive portion (316) comprises a second set of data paths (356A, 356B, 356C, 356D), wherein both the first set of data paths (336A-D) and second set of data paths (356A-D) are configurable to be aggregated or de-aggregated to support a single port (328A) operation that represents a combined bandwidth of the data paths in the first set of data paths (336A-D) or the second set of data paths (356A, 356B, 356C, 356D); wherein the receive portion (316) comprises a de-multiplexer (352, 448) that de-aggregates and distributes frames between the second set of data paths (356A-D).

2. The networking adaptor (104) of claim 1, wherein the transmit portion (312) comprises a multiplexer (332, 432) that connects the data paths in the first set of data paths (336A-D) to a number of different data ports (328A-D) that belong to the network interface (104); in particular wherein the multiplexer (332, 432) facilitates the aggregation of the data paths in the first set of data paths (336A-D).

3. The networking adaptor (104) of claim 2, wherein the multiplexer (332, 432) receives inputs from a set of transmission buffers (428), wherein the set of transmission buffers (428) couple the first set of data paths (336A-D) to the multiplexer (332, 432); in particular wherein the multiplexer (332, 432) aggregates the first set of data paths (336A-D) for a command based on an input key included in the command, wherein the input key comprises at least one of a work queue identifier and an exchange identifier along with a modulo operation that is applied to the input key.

4. The networking adaptor (104) of claim 3, wherein the multiplexer (332, 432) further comprises an egress arbiter (432) that is used to select and multiplex one of the data paths from the first set of data paths (336A-D) for frame transmission when a data path in the first set of data paths (336A-D) has at least one frame available to transmit in a round-robin fashion between the first set of data paths (336A-D).

5. The networking adaptor (104) of claim 1, wherein the de-multiplexer (352, 448) assigns and marks a serial number onto a beginning of each frame before the frame is de-multiplexed into one of the second set of data paths (356A-D); in particular wherein the de-multiplexer (352, 448) provides each frame to a set of receive buffers (444), wherein the set of receive buffers (444) couples the second set of data paths (356A-D) to the de-multiplexer (352, 448).

6. The networking adaptor (104) of claim 5, further comprising: a buffer manager (308, 408) that uses the serial number to reorder frames prior to providing the frames to the host interface (304, 404).
7. A method (500) of transferring commands from a host (108) to a network (112, 204), the method (500) comprising:
8. The method (500) of claim 7, wherein the one network port (328A) comprises a bandwidth that is a product of the first bandwidth and a number of data paths in the first set of data paths (336A-D).

9. The method (500) of claim 7 or 8, further comprising: placing the distributed command onto a plurality of transmission buffers (428) to ensure that the one network port can deliver a frame at the bandwidth provided by the one network port (436A).
10. A method (600) of transferring commands from a network (112, 204) to a host, the method comprising:
11. The method (600) of claim 10, further comprising: providing (612) the de-multiplexed frame to a set of receive buffers (444).
12. The method of claim 10 or 11, further comprising:
distributing (624) frames to multiple virtual output queues; in particular wherein an input key is used (628) for the distribution of the frames to the multiple virtual output queues.
13. The method (600) of claim 12, wherein the input key comprises at least one of a work queue identifier and an exchange identifier.
14. The method (600) of claim 13, wherein the input key is obtained from a frame header or a table lookup.

15. The method (600) of any of claims 10 to 14, wherein the host interface (304, 404) comprises a PCIe interface (404) and wherein the network port (348A-D) comprises a plurality of Fibre Channel (FC) ports.
